concept.name: Robustness test
concept.definition: A deliberately varied evaluation assessing whether a conclusion survives reasonable alternative data, periods, specifications, and implementation assumptions.
concept.intuition: It turns an informal trading idea into a claim or design choice that can be evaluated against dated evidence.
concept.mechanics: Prespecify credible alternatives, rerun the full analysis, report all outcomes, and distinguish stable signs from magnitude changes or failures.
concept.failure_modes: Results can mislead when hindsight, multiple testing, nonstationarity, costs, or unavailable historical information are ignored.
concept.misconceptions: A favorable historical result is evidence about the tested sample and assumptions, not proof of a durable profitable edge.
concept.example: A signal remains positive across equal-weight and volatility-weight portfolios but disappears when micro-cap stocks are excluded.

citations.source: CFA Institute Research Foundation, Investment Model Validation
